# Remodel

> Give any website a new look with one sentence.

Remodel is a Chrome extension. Open a website, type a style (for example "cyberpunk" or "neo-brutalist magazine"), and Remodel redesigns the page. Links, search, logins and forms keep doing what they did before.

The extension source is https://github.com/AbhineethVS/devin-hacks. This file describes the showcase site.

## Two ways it remodels

- Reskin, for most websites. Keeps the page exactly where it is and repaints colours, fonts, corner shapes and shadows. One model call returns a small theme, and a deterministic engine applies it. About 10 seconds. With the same fonts, nothing on the page moves. A theme made on one site applies instantly on another.
- Rebuild, for Wikipedia articles, Hacker News, and the IRCTC train-search page. Designs a new page from the content, with its own layout and scroll animations. The AI-written renderer runs in a sandbox with no extension access. After a rebuild, the AI looks at a screenshot of its own result and fixes obvious mistakes. On IRCTC, the new booking form still searches real trains.

## What else it does

- Suggest prompts: Remodel looks at the page and suggests three styles.
- Reuse a style: a style made on one site applies instantly on another.
- Before / after switch: press Alt+R to flip between the original and the new design.
- Remix a section: on Wikipedia, hover any section and restyle just that part.
- Watch it work: while it designs, five cursors visibly edit the page, retyping headings, moving blocks and picking colours.
- Self-check: after a rebuild, the AI reviews a screenshot of the result and fixes obvious mistakes.

## Before and after

These are real results from the extension. Image files are in `media/`.

- GitHub, prompt "cyberpunk / futuristic" (Reskin). The layout stays the same. Colours, fonts and shapes change. Before: `media/github-before.png`. After: `media/github-after-cyberpunk.png`.
- Wikipedia's Apple Inc. article (Rebuild). The whole page gets a new layout, in a clean Apple-keynote style. Before: `media/apple-wikipedia-before.png`. After: `media/apple-wikipedia-after.png`.
- Hacker News, as a retro desktop (Rebuild). The same live stories, inside a 90s-style computer window. Before: `media/hackernews-before.png`. After: `media/hackernews-after-windows95.png`.
- IRCTC train search, as a calm Japanese rail planner (Rebuild). The same booking form sits beside a station departures board listing every travel class. It still fills in IRCTC's real form, so searching shows real trains. The AI checked its own screenshot and fixed a mistake before the after shot. Before: `media/irctc-before.png`. After: `media/irctc-after-japanese-rail.png`.

## Demo videos

- python.org, pink neo-brutalist reskin: https://youtu.be/dNEG0L8O_Oc. Same page, repainted in loud pink with thick borders and heavy type.
- GitHub, neon reskin: https://youtu.be/Xa5lt1BeMjs. GitHub stays put. The colours and type turn neon.
- Wikipedia's Apple article, rebuilt: https://youtu.be/PlnK9Iw7WgI. The article gets a new layout, in a clean Apple-keynote style.
- Cyberpunk redesign: https://youtu.be/-1QaEpzxPYg. A page redesigned in a dark, neon Cyberpunk 2077 look.

## Install

1. Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode.
2. Click Load unpacked and choose the `extension` folder from https://github.com/AbhineethVS/devin-hacks.
3. Open any website and click Remodel in the bottom-right, or press Alt+Shift+M.
4. Paste an OpenAI API key. It stays in the browser.
5. Type a style and press Reskin this page, or Remodel this page on Wikipedia, Hacker News and IRCTC.

## Limits

- Pictures and logos keep their original colours, so a logo drawn for a light background can look off on a dark skin.
- On IRCTC, Remodel stops at train search. Login, booking and payment happen on the real IRCTC site.
- New fonts are metric-matched to the originals, but a line can occasionally re-wrap.
